title: Things to Do in Khajuraho: Chandela Temples, Light Show, Panna & Raneh Falls
seoTitle: Things to Do in Khajuraho: Temples, Panna & More | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Khajuraho: the Western Group of temples including Kandariya Mahadeva, the Eastern Jain temples, the Southern Group, the light and sound show, the Archaeological Museum, the Khajuraho Dance Festival, Panna National Park and Raneh Falls.
dek: A small village in Bundelkhand with some of the most celebrated temple sculpture in the world, built by the Chandela kings a thousand years ago.
searchIntent: Travellers planning one or two days in Khajuraho, often with Orchha or Panna.

intro: Khajuraho, in the Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh, was a religious centre of the Chandela dynasty, which built around 85 temples here between about 950 and 1050 CE. Around 25 survive, and together they were listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

The temples are famous for their sculpture: thousands of figures of gods, celestial dancers, musicians, warriors, animals and scenes of daily life, among which the erotic carvings are only a small part. The things to do in Khajuraho include the Western, Eastern and Southern groups of temples, the museum, the evening light show and, nearby, Panna National Park and the canyon at Raneh Falls.
One to two days is enough. October to March is the best time; the Khajuraho Dance Festival is held in February.
quickAnswer: Explore the Western Group of temples
See Kandariya Mahadeva, the largest temple
Visit the Jain temples of the Eastern Group
See Duladeo and Chaturbhuj in the Southern Group
Watch the light and sound show
Go on a safari in Panna National Park
See the canyon at Raneh Falls

items.name: Explore the Western Group
body: The Western Group, in a landscaped enclosure, holds the finest temples, including Lakshmana, Kandariya Mahadeva, Vishwanath, Chitragupta and Devi Jagadambi. Each stands on a high platform with rising towers meant to evoke Mount Kailash, and bands of carvings wrap around the walls. Hiring a licensed guide helps you read the sculptures.

Look for the sculptures of apsaras applying make-up, writing letters or removing thorns from their feet, and the friezes of armies, hunting scenes and processions along the plinths. The Lakshmana Temple is one of the best preserved, with a full set of subsidiary shrines at its corners.

items.name: See Kandariya Mahadeva
body: Kandariya Mahadeva, dedicated to Shiva, is the largest and most elaborate temple at Khajuraho, with over 800 sculptures and a tower about 31 metres high.

Walk around the temple clockwise to follow the carved bands, then look up at how the smaller towers climb towards the main spire, mirroring a mountain range. Late afternoon light brings out the depth of the carving.

items.name: Visit Matangeshwar Temple
body: Matangeshwar, next to the Western Group, is the only temple still in active worship, with a huge lingam. It is busy during Mahashivratri.

items.name: Watch the light and sound show
body: An evening light and sound show in the Western Group tells the story of the Chandelas and the temples, in English and Hindi.

items.name: Visit the Jain temples
body: The Eastern Group includes Jain temples such as Parsvanath, Adinath and Shantinath, with fine carvings, and Hindu temples such as Vamana and Javari.

items.name: See Duladeo and Chaturbhuj
body: The Southern Group has the Duladeo Temple, one of the last built, and the Chaturbhuj Temple, with a large carved image of Vishnu. They are quieter and good at sunset.

items.name: Visit the Archaeological Museum
body: The ASI museum opposite the Western Group has sculptures from the temples, including fine figures that were found loose around the site. It is closed on Fridays.

items.name: Attend the Khajuraho Dance Festival
body: Every February, the Khajuraho Dance Festival brings India's leading classical dancers to an open-air stage with the illuminated temples as backdrop.

items.name: Go on a safari in Panna
body: Panna National Park, about 25 km away, is a tiger reserve along the Ken river, where tigers were successfully reintroduced after they had disappeared. Jeep safaris and boat rides on the Ken are possible.
Pandav Falls, near the park, is a waterfall over a rock overhang with caves linked in legend to the Pandavas. The park is also good for vultures, crocodiles and birds along the river.

items.name: See Raneh Falls
body: Raneh Falls, about 20 km away, flows through a canyon of pink, red and grey granite. It is dramatic after the monsoon; in the dry season the rock formations themselves are the attraction. The Ken Gharial Sanctuary is nearby.

items.name: Cycle to nearby villages
body: Renting a bicycle to ride between temple groups and into the surrounding villages is a pleasant way to see rural Bundelkhand.

items.name: October to March
body: The best season for temples and safaris; the Dance Festival is in February.

items.name: April to June
body: Very hot; see the temples at dawn and dusk. Panna safaris have good sightings.

items.name: July to September
body: The monsoon brings green fields and full waterfalls; Panna's core zone is closed.

oneDay: Visit the Western Group at opening time with a guide, then the Archaeological Museum. After lunch, cycle to the Eastern and Southern groups, and return for the evening light and sound show.
tips: Khajuraho has a small airport and railway station; Jhansi is about four hours away.
Hire licensed guides at the ticket office.
Carry water and a hat; there is little shade.
Combine with Orchha and Panna for a longer trip.
Mornings are the best time for photography at the Western Group, before the crowds and heat.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Khajuraho?
faqs.a: See the Western, Eastern and Southern groups of temples, watch the light and sound show, visit the Archaeological Museum, attend the Dance Festival and visit Panna National Park and Raneh Falls.
No. Erotic sculptures are only a small part; most show gods, dancers, musicians, animals and daily life.
